MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  April 1, 2013

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Reardon at 5:02 p.m., on April 1, 2013, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on March 28, 2013, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Ury
  Council Member Leckness
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 5:12 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Reardon

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Ury

INVOCATION: Mayor Reardon

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of City
  Manager Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6

City Council Minutes  1  April 1, 2013
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:04 p.m., Mayor Reardon recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:05 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City Council addressed one personnel matter in
Closed Session. The Council provided direction but no reportable action occurred.

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Recognize the Mission Viejo Elks for their Generous Donation Towards the Purchase
  of a Replacement Canine for the Sheriff’s Department and Their Long Standing
  Support to our Community

  Mayor Reardon presented the certificate of appreciation to Exalted Ruler Harvey Boelts
  and introduced "Conan" the new Sheriff’s Department canine, along with Deputy Ryan
  Buhr.

P2. Recognize City Volunteers for Their 1,000 Hours of Service

  Mayor Reardon presented certificates of appreciation to (1) Margot Ferron for volunteer
  hours at the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center; (2) Septene McKinney for
  volunteer hours with the Mission Viejo Library; and (3) Karen Frazier, Geri Jones, Kim
  Brooks and Lynn Imus for volunteer hours at the Animal Services Center. Library
  volunteer Jack Naylor and Animal Services Center volunteer Carl Lekander were unable to
  attend the meeting.

P3. Presentation by The National Exchange Club

  The City Council received the presentation from Al K. Hicks of the South Orange County
  Exchange Club. Mr. Hicks announced that he is looking for six people to help start this
  Exchange Club branch and he invited those who are interested to contact him (949-280-
  6249.)

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that OCFA's unfunded liability has increased and he expressed
concern that financially strapped cities may have to withdraw from OCFA. If that occurs, he
believes that the remaining member cities will have to absorb the unfunded pension liability
portion of the withdrawn city.

Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: announced that the Mission Viejo Rotary Club will hold a fundraising
event on Saturday, April 6, 2013, at 5:30 p.m. at the Hills Hotel in Laguna Hills. She also

City Council Minutes  2  April 1, 2013
 reminded residents that the Elks club hosts bingo games on Wednesday evenings and she
encouraged residents to attend and support the Elks' efforts.

Joe Tully, M.V.: praised the City's Access MV mobile app which allows a resident to report an
issue as soon as they see it. He stated that it is an excellent tool and matters are acted upon very
quickly. Mr. Tully noted that you can also access the City newsletter and an "Ask the Mayor"
button from the app and he encouraged residents and homeowners associations to use it.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, and 11 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and
  further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for regular City Council meeting of March 18, 2013, as presented.

3.  Check Register Dated March 8, 2013 in the Amount of $2,014,173.30

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated March 15, 2013 in the Amount of $306,224.95

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

12. Purchase of Two Replacement Public Services Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) Fleet
  Vehicles.

  Awarded a purchase agreement for two Public Services CNG fleet vehicles to Tustin GMC
  in an amount not to exceed $92,828.16.

City Council Minutes  3  April 1, 2013
 13. Annual Routine Fleet Vehicle Repairs and Services

  (1) Approved Second Amendment to the existing contract with Mission Viejo Service
  Center, Inc. to increase current Fiscal Year 2012-13 purchase order by $15,000; (2)
  approved Third Amendment to the existing contract with Mission Viejo Service Center,
  Inc. for the period July 1, 2013, through June 30, 2015, to increase the contract amount by
  an amount not to exceed $106,200.00; and (3) authorized staff to issue a purchase order to
  Mission Viejo Service Center, Inc. for the period July 1, 2013, through June 30, 2014, in
  and amount not to exceed $53,100.00.

14. Local Hazard Mitigation Plan Update

  (1) Approved the agreement for consulting services with Glorria Morrison and Associates,
  Inc. in the amount of $34,800 for the update of the City's Local Hazard Mitigation Plan
  (LHMP); and (2) adopted Resolution 13-22 Amending the Fiscal Year 2012-13 Emergency
  Preparedness Budget for Expenses Related to the Pre-Disaster Mitigation Competitive
  Grant Program.

15. Mission Viejo Dog Park Annexation Process

  (1) Adopted Resolution 13-23 Authorizing the Local Agency Formation Commission of
  Orange County to Initiate the Process of Annexation for the Mission Viejo Dog Park; and
  (2) adopted Resolution 13-24 Approving the property Tax Exchange Agreement between
  the City of Mission Viejo and the City of Rancho Santa Margarita regarding the Arroyo
  Trabuco Openspace and the Mission Viejo Dog Park property line reorganization.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

Council Member Schlicht announced that she will be voting no on these contract amendments as
she feels that money is being taken from other areas to complete the Marguerite slopes and she
does not see any specific plan for getting all of the City's slopes done in a fair manner. She also
asked why there are no contract amendments for areas 1, 4 and 5.

Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay replied that Mariposa has opted
to not renew their contracts because they cannot afford to continue on and they are also worried
about future insurance costs. Staff will be going out to bid on those three contract areas.

Council Member Schlicht asked how many contracts staff would award to one contractor and
whether there is a limit in place.

City Council Minutes  4  April 1, 2013
 City Attorney Curley responded that City codes and state law require the City to award a contract
to the lowest responsible bidder. He would not recommend denying an agreement to that
contactor if there were no legitimate grounds.

Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to approve items 5
through 11 as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
NOES:  Schlicht
ABSENT:  None

5.  Annual Routine Monthly Landscape and Facility Maintenance - Contract Area 2

  (1) Approved First Amendment to the existing maintenance contract with Spectrum Care
  Landscape for the period July 1, 2013, through June 30, 2015, to increase the contract
  amount by an amount not to exceed $839,980.00; and (2) authorized staff to issue a
  purchase order to Spectrum Care Landscape for the period July 1, 2013, through June 30,
  2014, in an amount not to exceed $ 419,990.00.

6.  Annual Routine Monthly Landscape and Facility Maintenance - Contract Area 3

  (1) Approved Third Amendment to the existing maintenance contract with Spectrum Care
  Landscape, Inc. for the period of July 1, 2013, through June 30, 2015, to increase the
  contract amount by an amount not to exceed $598,700.00; and (2) authorized issuance of a
  purchase order to Spectrum Care Landscape, Inc. for the period of July 1, 2013, through
  June 30, 2014, in an amount not to exceed $299,350.00.

7.  Annual Routine Monthly Landscape and Facility Maintenance - Contract Area 6

  (1) Approved First Amendment to the existing maintenance contract with Vandergeest
  Landscape Care, Inc. for the period of July 1, 2013, through June 30, 2015, in the amount
  of $846,364.00; and (2) authorized issuance of a purchase order to Vandergeest Landscape
  Care, Inc. for the period of July 1, 2013, through June 30, 2014, in an amount not to exceed
  $423,182.00.

8.  Annual Routine Monthly Landscape and Facility Maintenance - Contract Area 7

  (1) Approved Second Amendment to the existing maintenance contract with Spectrum Care
  Landscape for the period July 1, 2013, through June 30, 2015, to increase the contract
  amount by an amount not to exceed $687,540.00; and (2) authorized staff to issue a
  purchase order to Spectrum Care Landscape for the period July 1, 2013, through June 30,
  2014, in an amount not to exceed $343,770.00.

City Council Minutes  5  April 1, 2013
 9.  Annual Routine Monthly Landscape and Facility Maintenance - Contract Area 8

  (1) Approved the First Amendment to the existing contract with Spectrum Care Landscape
  for the period of July 1, 2013, through June 30, 2015, to increase the contract amount by an
  amount not to exceed $1,039,746.00; and (2) authorized issuance of a purchase order to
  Spectrum Care Landscape for the period of July 1, 2013, through June 30, 2014, in an
  amount not to exceed $519,873.00.

10. Annual Routine Monthly Landscape and Facility Maintenance - Contract Area 9

  (1) Approved First Amendment to the existing contract with Spectrum Care Landscape for
  the period of July 1, 2013, through June 30, 2015, to increase the contract amount by an
  amount not to exceed $766,252.00; and (2) authorized issuance of a purchase order to
  Spectrum Care Landscape Inc. for the period of July 1, 2013, through June 30, 2014, in an
  amount not to exceed $383,126.00.

11. Annual Routine Monthly Landscape and Facility Maintenance - Contract Area 10

  (1) Approved First Amendment to the existing maintenance contract with Spectrum Care
  Landscape for the period July 1, 2013, through June 30, 2015, to increase the contract
  amount by an amount not to exceed $705,904.00; and (2) authorized staff to issue a
  purchase order to Spectrum Care Landscape for the period July 1, 2013, through June 30,
  2014, in an amount not to exceed $352,952.00.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

16. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: expressed his objection to the proposed OCFA policy
  amendment that would have limited public comments to 3 minutes per meeting instead of 3
  minutes per item. He also asked if the OCFA has undertaken a separate internal audit
  regarding inaccurate hazmat fees.

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

17. Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Reardon presented the report.

18. San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Reardon presented the report.

19. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury presented the report.
City Council Minutes  6  April 1, 2013
 20. Orange County Vector Control Board

  Council Member Leckness presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

21. Presentation, for City Council consideration and adoption, a Resolution entitled "A
  Resolution of the City Council of the City of Mission Viejo Making Determination of
  the City Council of the City of Mission Viejo Regarding San Onofre Nuclear
  Generating Station Restarting Units 2 and 3"

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  The following expressed support for the proposed resolution and an adjudicated hearing:
  Julie Tully, M.V.; Joe Tully, M.V.; and Joe Holtzman, M.V.

  Ellen Addonizio, M.V.: answered the Council's question regarding a similar resolution that
  was recently considered by the CUSD Board. She clarified that the CUSD Board tabled the
  resolution indefinitely.

  Frank Wasko, SCE: stated that SCE is asking the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC)
  to follow the standard regulatory process and to confirm their conclusions regarding safety.
  Mr. Wasko answered the City Council Members questions.

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley recommended that her colleagues visit the Southern California
  Association of Governments (SCAG) website to view the energy presentations that are
  posted there. She noted that she will send the Council Members a direct link for their
  convenience.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to adopt
  Resolution 13-XX Making Determinations Regarding San Onofre Nuclear Generating
  Station Restarting Units 2 and 3, including the Council's urging that the NRC require
  Edison to undergo a public, transparent adjudicated license amendment hearing.

  AMENDED motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury,
  to direct staff to resend, by fax, the letter that was dated August 9, 2012, and provide a
  cover memo restating the City Council's safety concerns and recapping the discussion of
  tonight. The correspondence will not urge the NRC to conduct an adjudicated hearing.

  On roll call, said AMENDED motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, and Ury
  NOES:  Reardon and Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  7  April 1, 2013
 RECESS

At the hour of 9:24 p.m., Mayor Reardon declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 9:33
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

City Manager’s Report

City Attorney’s Report

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

22. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended
  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Leckness

Council Member Leckness outlined his attendance at recent events including the Chamber
breakfast, "zombie day" at La Paz Intermediate School and Bunny Days where he worked as a
face painter.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht reminded residents that Al Hicks is starting a South Orange County
Exchange Club which does charitable work, mainly for children. Mr. Hicks can be reached at
(949) 280-6249 or ahicks2000@cox.net. Council Member Schlicht concluded her comments
with a Yiddish proverb: "A half-truth is a whole lie."

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury had no comments and he informed the Mayor that he had to leave the
meeting. Mr. Ury departed at 9:38 p.m.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley announced that the cities of Mission Viejo and Aliso Viejo paid for the
lion's share of the Capistrano Unified School District offices building. The cities CFD 87-1
Mello Roos dollars paid $14.3 million out of $19.8 million and she will be asking about this in
the upcoming ad hoc committee meeting with CUSD. She noted that she is very concerned and
she may be requesting an audit similar to the one the City requested in 2006; however her first
step will be to talk to CUSD representative about the matter. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley discussed
her attendance at the Medal of Valor ceremony where four Mission Viejo deputies were honored
with lifesaving medals. She stated that it is such a good feeling to hear the stories of how each of
these Sheriff's department personnel has impacted a life. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley announced that
there will be a Red Cross blood drive on Friday, April 5, 2013, in the Saddleback Room at City
Hall from 12:00 to 6:00 p.m. She also reminded her colleagues that she will miss the April 15
City Council Minutes  8  April 1, 2013
 Council Meeting because she will be helping her daughter with a move to Minnesota. Lastly,
Mayor Pro Tem Kelley announced that the Community of Character word for the month of April
is service.

Mayor Reardon

Mayor Reardon announced that the recent Chamber of Commerce breakfast was excellent. Lucy
Dunn from Orange County Business Council presented some great information and Senator
Mark Wyland was interesting as he expressed his frustration that he could not accomplish what
he set out to do in Sacramento regarding the State's educational system. Mayor Reardon read the
same information that she had presented at the Chamber breakfast on the City's Economic
Development Committee's efforts to evaluate the future and trends of businesses in the
community. She also discussed her attendance at the Medal of Valor ceremony and she
announced that the City Council will be honoring the four Mission Viejo deputies who received
lifesaving medals, at an upcoming Council Meeting. Mayor Reardon further outlined her
attendance at the South Orange County Mayor's Association meeting which Mission Viejo
recently hosted. City Manager Wilberg had recommended that they address the prescription drug
problem in South Orange County and she stated that it was one of the best meetings they have
had in years. Mayor Reardon discussed her attendance at Bunny Days where she met a woman
and her two daughters who had just moved to Mission Viejo from Australia after they fell in love
with this family-oriented community. She also recently met a family that has moved here from
San Francisco and they too love the City.

Council Member Leckness let Mayor Reardon know that he has heard from several people how
great she was at the Chamber breakfast. She was an excellent speaker and did a nice job
highlighting local businesses and business owners.

Mayor Reardon thanked Council Member Leckness for the compliment and she thanked City
staff for the list of businesses that they helped her with; both new companies and those that have
been in existence since the 1970s.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:51 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Reardon adjourned the meeting to Monday, April 15, 2013, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of April 15, 2013

City Council Minutes  9  April 1, 2013
